Where pupils dare to know
“An outstandingly happy and successful school”
Independent School in Hampshire
Our School is a happy and thriving learning environment for children aged 4 to 16 years. At the centre of our ethos is strong pastoral care, where each individual is treated with respect and dignity.
At Rookwood your child is encouraged to think and to question for themselves, allowing them to flourish from a very young age right through to sixth form.
Our school motto is ‘Sapere Aude’ which can be translated as ‘dare to know’ or ‘have courage to understand’ and it certainly captures the essence of our identity as a school.

Nursery School
Our youngest children begin their intrepid learning journey in Little Rooks, a happy, peaceful and nurturing setting. The early years are so important, as they provide the foundation for life; not just academically but socially and emotionally. We pride ourselves at Rookwood on developing the whole child within a stimulating learning environment, supported by caring staff dedicated to giving children the best start in education.
Prep School
Our Prep School is small enough to ensure that each child is known to all members of staff and is valued as an individual. We know their likes and dislikes, what their strengths are and how we can best support them on their academic journey. Our children are encouraged to take advantage of the countless opportunities presented to them and to grow as individuals academically, socially and emotionally.
Senior School
Rookwood’s senior school has a reputation for being a friendly and caring school which also achieves excellent exam results. Our nurturing approach is conveyed by staff, evident in the environment and reflective in the pupils’ wellbeing and progress.
Our pupils become resilient and capable learners, able to tackle life’s challenges with integrity and a generosity of spirit. At Rookwood, your child will become the best version of themselves.
Boarding
Boarding at Rookwood is a unique experience and is refreshingly different from traditional boarding. Our boarding houses are very much ‘homes from home’, which provide a secure and familiar environment to enjoy being with friends and make use of the school facilities for evening activities. With excellent adult:child ratios, our houseparents get to know each boarder as an individual, providing the strong pastoral care for which Rookwood boarding is renowned.

Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
About
Rookwood School sits on an eight-acre site just a short walk from Andover town centre and railway station.
Whilst Rookwood has changed over the 90 years since it was first formed, we continue to place a real emphasis on traditional core values.
Courtesy, good manners, kindness and respect for those around us are all essential components of life at Rookwood.
The Rookwood way
At Rookwood, we recognise that every child is unique and has their own specific strengths and talents, as well as areas for development. Therefore we do not adopt a ‘one-size-fits-all’ approach to our education but, instead, we get to know every child and tailor our provision accordingly.
When parents tour the school, they immediately notice small classes where pupils receive constant focus and attention, mutual respect between pupils themselves and with staff, as well as the passion teachers have for developing and nurturing every child.
No matter what, we bring out the very best in your child.

pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Welcome from the Head
Welcome to Rookwood School
We are a school which values each child as an individual, fosters a love of learning and, above all, is a happy place to learn.
As a non-selective school, we do not ‘cherry-pick’ those children who happen to do well in a set of exams when they were young. However, we do expect the very best from our pupils. This philosophy is not about reaching potential, it is about growing potential: giving our pupils the opportunities and encouragement to help them understand that they can achieve much more than they first realise.
Rookwood’s motto, sapere aude, translated as ‘dare to know’, is clearly seen in everything we do. Our pupils are challenged to have courage, to learn new things, to develop new skills and to deepen their understanding. As a result, our pupils leave Rookwood with the essential character traits of integrity, tenacity and respect for others, and with excellent exam results.
To really understand what we do, I encourage you to visit us and see for yourself.
Mr Paul Robinson Headteacher
P.S. You may like to read my latest blog posts, where I share regular reflections on life at Rookwood School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum for Years 1 & 2 | Rookwood School | Primary School Andover
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Curriculum (Years 1-2)
Developing independent learners
In Years 1 and 2, children follow a thematic curriculum, led by their classroom teacher. The key learning skills of literacy, numeracy, creativity and curiosity are all developed through the study of the half-termly topics.
Stimulating natural curiosity
We recognise that the transition from Reception to Year 1 needs to be smooth, to provide continuity and consistency for the children. Our teachers spend time in both settings during key points in the year, to ensure that your child will be well prepared and ready to embark on the next phase of their learning. Our close, nurturing environment across the School ensures that teachers know your child well before they join them in the later years.
Rookwood creates in inquiry-based learning environment for children in this key stage, designed to stimulate a natural curiosity for their new environment. Learning themes such as ‘where we learn’ enable our teachers to introduce the subjects of History, Geography, Science, Design Technology and The Arts.
The timetable also consists of Music, PE and French which are taught by specialist teachers. The children’s learning is deepened by the opportunity to spend time in the library, the pastoral nest, visits from external speakers and authors, day trips to places such as Marwell Zoo.
The curriculum is designed to develop independent learners who take pride in their own learning and who can work as part of a team as much as striving to do their best themselves.
At this important formative developmental stage for children, communication with parents is vital. We pride ourselves on a triangle relationship between the staff, children and parents which ensures that the children are involved in all aspects of their learning and assessments. Parents are encouraged to support their child’s learning through regular reading at home.
Rookwood offers many formal and informal opportunities throughout the school year for parents and teachers to share insights and observations of how the children are settling in and thriving throughout the year. Our wrap-around care is a daily privilege made even stronger by enthusiastic and consistent communication at parents’ evenings, learning journey sessions, within formal reports and the informal chats at school drop off and pick up.

pageCache.pageTitle: Years 3-6 Curriculum | Rookwood School | Hampshire Prep School
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Curriculum (Years 3-6)
Our school motto comes to life in the Prep School – we dare to learn!
The curriculum for children in our Prep School, for Years 3 to 6, is engaging, varied and above all… a fun adventure! The subjects explored in the thematic curriculum are English, Maths, Arts, Sciences, Humanities, Languages, ICT and Sports alongside ‘Philosophy 4 Children’ (P4C) and Personal, Social & Health Education (PSHE), which all ensure our children are experiencing a huge range of topics as well as developing their moral, social and spiritual understanding and learning essential life skills. The pupils’ learning is deepened by the opportunity to spend time in the library, the pastoral nest, have visits from external speakers and authors, enjoy day trips and experience fun residential outings too!
Developing independence
Our Prep School curriculum is designed to develop independent learners who take pride in their own learning and work and who can work as part of a team, as much as striving to do their best themselves. The children in Prep School move around to specialist classrooms and to be taught by specialist teachers for a number of their lessons and this furthers their independence as well as enabling them to be in subject appropriate environments.
Sharing the adventure with parents
Parents and families of Rookwood are welcome into the adventure – strong home partnerships creates this shared experience. Exciting projects come to life when our pupils are empowered to share their journey with parents and with the progress of each child being demonstrated through the enthusiasm they convey when talking about their learning discoveries which compliments our careful tracking and observations of their progress made in each year.
A learning journey to be shared
A triangle relationship between the staff, children and parents of Rookwood ensures that the children are involved in all aspects of their learning and assessments. More formally there are once yearly parents’ evenings and regular written reports, but we very much welcome regular involvement and conversations about each childs’ experience of school and the adventure of this, shown by our motivated and engaged pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Curriculum | Early Years Learning at Little Rooks | Andover
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Nursery Curriculum
A Wholesome Balance of Learning & Development
Our caring specialist nursery teachers are knowledgeable, skilled and experienced in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum for children aged between six months to four years old, providing a great introduction for your child’s education at Rookwood School. Daily activities are planned to foster the three prime areas of childhood development: personal, social and emotional development, communication and language development, and the physical development of your child. We pride ourselves on providing a wholesome balance of these areas so that your child feels valued for their unique contribution to the community no matter what stage of development they begin school life with.
Learning through Safe Exploration
Our children learn in a supported exploratory way that nurtures participation, fun and independence, with teachers offering creative ways to introduce literacy, mathematics, world exploration, and the expressive arts and design. Additionally, during our morning sessions, the children also enjoy extra learning activities such as French, Dance and PE with specialist teachers that slowly introduces them to other parts of the school so that they feel familiar, connected and confident in the school environment and confident to follow their joy and interests that emerge as they discover themselves and their interests.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception Curriculum | Rookwood School | Primary School in Andover
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Curriculum (Reception)
The best possible start in life
The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum (EYFS) provides children with the skills necessary to have the best possible start to life. Here, your child will embrace and direct their learning through a combination of play-based and adult supported learning.
Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum (EYFS)
The four specific EYFS areas of learning are: Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding the World and Expressive Arts and Design.
Rookwood’s Reception children follow a creative curriculum filled with awe and wonder. Your child will be encouraged to become an independent explorer who engages with their environment. A focus on personal and social development is key in developing happy individuals with a sense of belonging and self-efficacy. Each child is valued, with learning experiences tailored to their development, interests and needs.
“Our daughter joined Rookwood at Reception class and has thrived in her first year developing lots of confidence. She has benefited from a small class size and excellent staff and resources. “
Parent of Reception child (2025)
A learning journey to be shared
Teaching and learning is very much a joint partnership where teachers share these responsibilities with your child. Through connecting learning areas with exciting topics, the children express their interests and direct the learning to make it meaningful, fun and purposeful. Opportunities for problem-solving and challenge-based learning are incorporated into the daily routine, allowing your child to extend their skills and deepen their understanding. We acknowledge the importance and value of parents to our children’s wellbeing and learning. Therefore, we proactively work with parents in delivering the best possible education for our children.
The time spent in Reception is truly magical, with your child building positive attitudes and relationships towards their learning and others. Rookwood provides this magical feel.
Developing the whole child
Our Reception curriculum develops the whole child. A child’s sense of self and belonging is vital in the early years. We ensure that each child is cared for, feeling nurtured and valued. Socially, carpet time sessions are held in order to discuss challenges relevant to them where their peers can support and brainstorm solutions to real life problems.
At Rookwood, your child will be given plenty of opportunities to develop their balance and motor-skills. The Reception setting consists of a large classroom and an outdoor area where the children can use their bodies to explore their surroundings and undertake exciting and fun challenges. Children also have four dedicated PE lessons each week, including dance all year round and swimming in the summer, with specialist teachers.
Rookwood’s Reception provides a language-rich environment which encourages children to use a wide vocabulary within their play. Your child will read to an adult daily and engage in story-telling activities on a regular basis. Adults value the children’s interests, joining in with children’s natural play to ensure that new vocabulary and language is modeled. This allows for consolidation and deep understanding of concepts to occur. The weekly French and Music lessons also help develop your child’s communication and language skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular Activities | Rookwood Prep School | Andover
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Extra-Curricular
Prep School opportunites
Rookwood has always understood that developing a child is about so much more than academic success. With over 100 weekly extracurricular clubs in a typical term, we offer a wide variety of opportunities to help develop a child’s confidence, resilience and strength of character.
Fully inclusive opportunities
Our all-embracing inclusive approach ensures that every child feels secure and supported, giving them the courage to tackle new opportunities and discover talents they didn’t know they possessed. In the Prep School, we offer children exciting challenges such as the Prince William Award, charity fundraisers, drama productions, sports, arts, technology clubs and more. Above all, the choice is created by the imagination and enthusiasm of our pupils – which is limitless!
Clubs, trips and outside adventures
Resilience, teamwork, independence and risk taking are all qualities we develop within Rookwood children. Therefore, clubs, trips and residential visits are all a huge part of school life and they are always fun! There is a vast termly clubs programme which gives the children the opportunity to take part in a range of activities such as chess, trampolining, mine craft, art, eco committee, multi sports, choir and many more. Every term to reinforce the classroom learning and deepen the understanding of the topics the children are visited or visit places such as the Sea City Museum, Pizza Express, Windsor Castle, The Roman Baths, author visits and theatre groups.
Community Participation
Throughout the year the Prep School is fully immersed in themed events such as Science week, Maths day, Queens Jubilee and Book Day. The children in Years 4, 5 and 6 spend 4 days on a residential trip each year testing their courage, putting themselves outside of their comfort zones, experiencing new things and developing their independence. This is a favourite week for staff and children

pageCache.pageTitle: Visit Rookwood School | Tours & Open Days | Best School in Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Tours & Open Days
Experience Rookwood
The best way to find out more about Rookwood School is to experience it for yourself. We offer Open Mornings throughout the year, as well as Taster Days for potential pupils to experience what life at Rookwood would be like for themselves.
We would also be happy to arrange a tour of the independent school on a day that suits you and offer 1:1 appointments to meet our Headteacher directly.
Open Events
Our Open Mornings offer the chance to experience Rookwood School in a relaxed and authentic way. They begin with a welcome from our Headteacher, Mr Robinson, followed by a personalised tour led by two of our pupils, who share their own stories and experiences. Along the way, you will meet our staff, explore our facilities and gain a real insight into the academic challenge, pastoral care and opportunities that help every pupil thrive.
Our next School Open Morning will take place in Spring 2027, with the date to be announced soon.
In the meantime, we warmly encourage families to book a personalised tour with our Admissions team. This is a wonderful opportunity to explore our welcoming school, meet our staff and discover what makes Rookwood such a special place to learn and grow. Please contact our Admissions Team to arrange your visit. We would be delighted to welcome you!
Taster Days
If you’ve decided that you would like to consider Rookwood School for your child, and once you have registered your child’s place, we would love to offer a Taster Day. Our Taster Days give your child the chance to see what it would be like to be part of the Rookwood family and experience the school, meet staff and interact with their fellow pupils for themselves. Please contact our Admissions team to schedule a taster day.
Each year, we also run a group Taster Day for pupils interested in joining Rookwood School into Year 7. Our Year 7 Discovery Day will take place on Tuesday 17th November. If you would like to attend, please contact our Admissions team at admissions@rookwoodschool.org.
1:1 meetings with the Head
If our Open Mornings are not convenient for you, then we are happy to offer 1:1 meetings with our Headteacher, Mr Paul Robinson, at a time that suits you. Please get in touch with us to arrange this.

pageCache.pageTitle: A memorable international experience - Rookwood School
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
A memorable international experience
We were delighted to welcome a group of Year 9 and 10 students from Argentina to Rookwood for a two-week immersion experience. During their stay, the students fully immersed themselves in life at Rookwood, joining lessons, exploring the local area and experiencing day-to-day school life alongside our pupils.
As part of their visit, the students also prepared and delivered presentations on Argentinian music and food, giving our pupils a wonderful opportunity to learn more about another culture and celebrate international perspectives together.
Experiences such as this broaden horizons, build confidence and foster meaningful cultural exchange, enriching the learning experience for everyone involved. As we reflect on their visit, we are delighted to share some of the students’ own feedback and memories from their time at Rookwood.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep School teachers take on the Shine Night Walk - Rookwood School
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Prep School teachers take on the Shine Night Walk
At the end of term, our wonderful Prep School team took part in Cancer Research UK’s Shine Night Walk in Southampton, completing an inspiring 10km charity challenge and raising an incredible £1,820!
The walk held a special significance for our school community, as the team came together in loving memory of our much-missed Prep School Head, Elaine Ozanne, who sadly passed away last year. Elaine touched the lives of so many people at Rookwood, and taking part in this event was a heartfelt way to honour her memory and celebrate the lasting impact she made.
A huge thank you to everyone who walked, donated and supported this wonderful cause. We are incredibly proud of our team for coming together to make a difference and ensure that every step counted.

pageCache.pageTitle: Rookwood Celebrates a Successful Open Morning - Rookwood School
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Rookwood Celebrates a Successful Open Morning
We were delighted to welcome a record number of prospective families to Rookwood for our recent Open Morning. The event provided an opportunity to showcase our school, the curriculum and the many opportunities available to our pupils. I have, however, always believed that what truly distinguishes our school is our wonderful people.
Throughout the morning, the warmth of our community and the genuine hospitality extended to visitors were clear to see. Our pupils were exemplary, speaking with confidence, enthusiasm and sincerity, and representing everything that makes Rookwood such a fantastic school. The feedback from visiting families was overwhelmingly positive, with many commenting on the happiness of our pupils and staff, the positive relationships they observed and the sense of belonging throughout the School. These are not qualities that can simply be switched on for an Open Morning. They are developed carefully over many years through the nurturing of relationships, the consistent modelling of values and the everyday interactions that shape our sense of community. Equally important is the enjoyment we share in working with young people, something I see reflected in the laughter, enthusiasm and positive working relationships across Rookwood every day.
My sincere thanks go to our pupils, colleagues and all our families for making Rookwood a community of which we can all be very proud!

pageCache.pageTitle: Outstanding Exam Results | Rookwood School | GCSE & A-Level Results
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Exam Results
Year on year success
Rookwood School maintains a strong track record for exam success at GCSE and A Level and we are incredibly proud of every student that passes through Rookwood’s doors.
GCSE Results 2026
Our Year 11 students celebrated an excellent set of GCSE results in August, marking the culmination of years of hard work, determination and commitment.
A quarter of grades were awarded at grades 7–9, equivalent to the former A/A* grades, with 13% achieving the very highest grades of 8 or 9.
Headteacher, Mr Paul Robinson, said the results reflected not only the academic achievements of the students, but also the determination and resilience they have shown throughout their time at Rookwood.
The results mark an important milestone for Year 11 students, who have been supported throughout their final year to identify the right next step for them. As they move on to a range of leading sixth forms and colleges, each student leaves Rookwood ready to pursue a pathway that reflects their individual strengths, interests and ambitions.
We warmly congratulate all of students on their excellent achievements and wish them every success as they move forward in their education.
RESULTS BREAKDOWN 2026
RESULTS BREAKDOWN 2025
RESULTS BREAKDOWN 2024
RESULTS BREAKDOWN 2023
A Level Results 2026
Our recent Sixth Form students celebrated exceptional A Level results, with 60% of all grades awarded at A*- B, and 80% A – C with a 100% pass rate across all subjects.
Rookwood students further excelled in creative subjects including Fine Art, Textile Design and Photography, with 100% of grades awarded A* - A - an outstanding achievement and testament to the exceptional talent, creativity and dedication of the students and teachers.
Strong results were also achieved across the wider curriculum, including subjects such as Design & Technology and Geography; as well as the school’s vocational provision, with 100% pass rate at Distinction in BTEC Level 3 Sport.
In addition to these superb grades, our students achieved conditional offers for their university applications, meaning our students secured their first-choice university destinations.
Mr Robinson, Headteacher, said: ”We are incredibly proud of our students and all they have achieved. These results reflect not only their academic ability, but the determination, creativity and resilience they have demonstrated throughout their time at Rookwood.
“Our school motto, Sapere Aude – Dare to Know, encourages our students to be curious, to challenge themselves and to have the confidence to pursue their individual talents and ambitions. These results are a wonderful reflection of that spirit, with excellent achievements across academic, creative and vocational subjects. As our leavers take their next steps, we hope they continue to Dare to Know, embrace new opportunities and achieve more than they ever thought possible.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating outstanding A-Level Success - Rookwood School
pageCache.text:
Insight and inspiration from our Headteacher: Read his latest blogs.
Celebrating outstanding A-Level Success
Rookwood School celebrates A Level success in 2026
Thursday 13th August, 2026
Rookwood School is proud to announce another exceptional set of A Level results today, reflecting the commitment, talent, and resilience of our students. This year, 60% of all grades awarded were at A*- B, and 80% A – C with a 100% pass rate across all subjects.
Rookwood students further excelled in creative subjects including Fine Art, Textile Design and Photography, with 100% of grades awarded A* - A - an outstanding achievement and testament to the exceptional talent, creativity and dedication of the students and teachers.
Strong results were also achieved across the wider curriculum, including subjects such as Design & Technology and Geography; as well as the school’s vocational provision, with 100% pass rate at Distinction in BTEC Level 3 Sport.
In addition to these superb grades, our students achieved conditional offers for their university applications, meaning our students secured their first-choice university destinations.
Mr Robinson, Headteacher, said: ”We are incredibly proud of our students and all they have achieved. These results reflect not only their academic ability, but the determination, creativity and resilience they have demonstrated throughout their time at Rookwood.
“Our school motto, Sapere Aude – Dare to Know, encourages our students to be curious, to challenge themselves and to have the confidence to pursue their individual talents and ambitions. These results are a wonderful reflection of that spirit, with excellent achievements across academic, creative and vocational subjects. As our leavers take their next steps, we hope they continue to Dare to Know, embrace new opportunities and achieve more than they ever thought possible.”
Among those celebrating was Zac, who secured his place at the University of East Anglia, to study Energy Engineering. Zac was thrilled with his results and said, ‘I thought I hadn’t done enough, but have checked my email and I’m in.’ Zac will start university in September and says that ‘he is excited and nervous about his next steps.’ We wish him every success and look forward to hearing about how he gets on.
Rookwood School is a co-educational independent school with day and boarding provision in Andover, Hampshire. The school prides itself on providing a personalised education in which students are known as individuals, supported by experienced teachers and encouraged to pursue their own interests, talents and aspirations.
As students now prepare to move on to their next chapters, the whole Rookwood community celebrates their achievements and wishes them every success for the future.
Dare to Know. Dare to achieve.
